copies.headline: John's Rams Stack Can't Cover the Backfield Gap
copies.body:
This gets decided at running back, where Noah is holding De'Von Achane and James Cook III (34 projected for the top two) against Kyren Williams and D'Andre Swift at 26. Achane's game is the ugliest on the board — Miami at Las Vegas, 40.5 total, three-point dog — but a trailing Dolphins offense funnels through him anyway, and Cook is in a 44.5-total coin flip in Houston where Buffalo needs him. John's counter is a Rams stack: Stafford, Kyren and Puka Nacua in a 48.5 against San Francisco, the best real game either side owns. Nacua at 21 is genuinely the top single player here.
The problem is what's behind it. Brock Bowers is doubtful, which turns a tight end edge into Trey McBride and nothing, and Keaton Mitchell is questionable in a room that doesn't need him. John's WR3 slot is Brian Thomas Jr. or Quentin Johnston at 10 — fine, not scary. Noah's receiving room is thin and Jordyn Tyson is on IR, but the back-end depth and two usable defenses cover more ground than John's, and #6 versus #11 in the power rankings isn't an accident.

copies.headline: Isaac's Receivers Can't Cover Every Hole
copies.body:
Isaac wins receiver and loses everywhere else, which is a bad trade when the everywhere-else includes quarterback and both running back slots. Ja'Marr Chase in a 50.5-total game against Tampa is the single best asset on the field, and McLaurin, Metcalf and a questionable Malik Nabers give him a real three-deep. But Bo Nix at Kansas City in a 43.5 total is the lowest-ceiling starting quarterback in this game by a wide margin, and Malik Willis in a 40.5 total isn't a pivot. Behind him: Javonte Williams and Cam Skattebo in the same 48.5-point Cowboys-Giants game, then nothing.
Kaleb's edge is boring and structural — Herbert as a 9.5-point home favorite, Ashton Jeanty getting volume against Miami, Breece Hall in a game the Jets will likely be chasing. Harold Fannin Jr. beats either Hockenson or Kincaid at tight end. Isaac is 12th in the power rankings for exactly this reason: one elite position, four soft ones.

copies.headline: CJ's Backfield Is a Hospital Wing
copies.body:
Receiver decides this one. Grant's top three go for 45 against CJ's 40, and the gap is really about floor: Amon-Ra St. Brown gets Detroit as a seven-point home favorite in a 50.5-point game, the best script on either roster, while CJ leans on Rashee Rice and Emeka Egbuka with Alec Pierce questionable behind them. Egbuka at least lands in the same Cincinnati shootout that makes Joe Burrow the one clear CJ edge, worth two on Kyler Murray in a 46.5-total division game.
The running backs tie at 31 on paper, but CJ's depth chart is a casualty report — TreVeyon Henderson and Zach Charbonnet out, Isiah Pacheco on IR. One Jonathan Taylor tweak and he's starting MarShawn Lloyd. Grant has Omarion Hampton against Arizona with the Chargers laying 9.5, plus Tony Pollard and Jadarian Price in reserve. Zay Flowers questionable is Grant's only real worry, and Christian Watson and Chris Godwin cover it.

copies.headline: Logan's Eagles Stack Meets Adam's Fragile Backfield
copies.body:
The Philadelphia game is the whole thing. Logan owns both sides of the Eagles offense in Jalen Hurts (21) and Saquon Barkley (18) against a Washington defense that's a 5.5-point road underdog, and Adam is on the other end of it with Jayden Daniels chasing in a 44.5-total game that projects tight and low-scoring rather than open. That's a four-point QB gap on paper and a wider one if Philly leads and Barkley grinds out the fourth quarter. Logan's edge at running back is real too: Adam's best two are Kenneth Walker III (15) in a 43.5-total Chiefs game and Rico Dowdle (12) behind a modest Pittsburgh total.
Adam's counter is receiver depth, and it's thin at the top rather than wide — Jaxon Smith-Njigba (19) and Chris Olave (15), whose Saints are seven-point dogs in a 50.5 shootout, plus a questionable Rome Odunze. Two points at wideout and two at tight end don't cover nine elsewhere. Logan can also absorb a Jeremiyah Love scratch with Dobbins and five viable wideouts; Adam can't absorb a Walker dud.

copies.headline: Peter's Depth Chart Is Held Together By Question Marks
copies.body:
The top-line numbers say this is a coin flip — Peter wins QB by two with Lamar Jackson in a 47.5-total game at Indianapolis, Christian wins receiver by two — but coin flips are decided underneath, and that's where Peter is exposed. A.J. Brown and Jalen McMillan are both questionable, which drags Tee Higgins (50.5 in Cincinnati, the best number on either roster) from luxury to necessity, and if Brown sits, the WR3 is Jalen Nailor at nine. Behind Bijan Robinson, who's playing in a 42.5-total game in Pittsburgh as an underdog, sits a questionable Jonathon Brooks and Kyle Monangai. Tucker Kraft is a fine tight end but the margin there is one point.
Christian's edge is that nothing has to break right. Chase Brown gets the 50.5 with Cincinnati, Travis Etienne is in a Detroit game projected for 50.5 as a seven-point dog that throws late, and Bhayshul Tuten is a genuine RB3 at 13. CeeDee Lamb and DeVonta Smith are both favored. George Kittle in a game with no posted line is the one soft spot, and Christian can absorb it.

copies.headline: Leif's Running Backs Outlast Mitchell's Quarterback Experiment
copies.body:
Leif wins this in the backfield and at quarterback, which is a nice place to have your edges. Christian McCaffrey and Derrick Henry are 35 projected points before you get to David Montgomery, and Henry lands in Indianapolis as a 3.5-point favorite in a 47.5 game — exactly the script where Baltimore leans on him in the fourth quarter. Josh Allen at Houston in a 44.5 total isn't a fireworks show, but Allen's floor is other people's ceiling. Mitchell's answer at quarterback is Jaxson Dart against Dallas, a 3-point home dog in a 48.5 game, which at least means volume. It also means a rookie deciding your week.
Mitchell's real strength is receiver, where Nico Collins, Courtland Sutton and DJ Moore top Leif's trio by four, plus a two-point edge at tight end with Tyler Warren. That's six points of cushion against seven points of RB and QB. The problem is behind Jahmyr Gibbs: Josh Jacobs is day-to-day at zero, Rachaad White and Chris Brooks are single-digit filler, and Tank Dell is on IR. Gibbs in a 50.5 total against New Orleans has to carry it alone. Leif's Mahomes tag is the only crack, and he doesn't need him.

intro: Christian at Peter is the one worth watching all afternoon — two rosters built the same way, heavy at the top and thin behind it, so whichever bench spot cracks first decides it. Grant at CJ is the opposite problem: Grant walks in with the deeper skill group at every position that matters, and CJ needs the kind of Week 1 chaos that usually only helps the other guy. Everything else lands somewhere in between, which in Week 1 means we're all just guessing with extra confidence.
